I've never liked Twitter and am unsurprised that it continues to slide. The fact that the service is predicated on the artificiality of 140 characters has always struck me as ridiculous (yes I'm aware it started as an SMS-service and that they're finally planning on expanding the length). But that artificiality is what primarily set it apart from other social media. Mainstream media has pushed Twitter hard with every network urging viewers to follow specific shows and live-tweet. Obviously this is a form of "engagement" but I've seen little evidence that it has grown in popularity. I know tons of people (like me) who opened a Twitter account to see what it was about, but rarely, if ever, participate. Contrast that with other services like Instagram which have continued to keep growing. The twitter communities I do occasionally visit are cesspools in which warring factions do nothing but attack each other. These antics don't speak favorably of the service.

Finally, although I do agree with the OP that Twitter censorship is a big negative, I find it highly inappropriate to editorialize/soapbox in the title of a thread. I don't even disagree with you. But Voat really needs to get this soapboxing in check. Voat would seem far less like a right-wing, racist, gun-nut cesspool if folks quit posting threads with loaded rhetoric in big subs like /v/technology.
